title: Consolidate Conditional Expression

solutions.title: One name for the three that agree, one guard for the one that doesn't
solutions.tradeoff: isPriorityCase reads as a single rule instead of three, but isEligibleForSameDaySlot now has to say out loud that a fourth condition is deliberately excluded from it - a reader who only skims isPriorityCase and assumes it is the whole story will miss the paging.

reviewFocus: Do the three merged conditions actually share one consequence and no side effects, or did a fourth get folded in by pattern-matching on shape alone?
Is pageOnCallNurseIfFlagged still called unconditionally, or did it end up inside the || chain where short-circuiting could skip it?
Does the OnCallLog assertion in the tests actually distinguish the correct solution from a naive isPriorityCase(patient) || pageOnCallNurseIfFlagged(patient, log) merge?
Is isPriorityCase named for what it answers, or does it just restate 'the three conditions that got merged'?
Would a reviewer, reading only isEligibleForSameDaySlot, know that a nurse gets paged as a side effect of calling it?
